subject: Human Body
title: ADH and Water Balance
description: A quick, practical guide to ADH and Water Balance.

hook.text: Dehydrated? Your brain detects it and tells your kidneys to hold onto water. The messenger is ADH.

buildup.text: ADH (antidiuretic hormone) is made in the hypothalamus and stored in the pituitary.

discovery.text: When blood becomes concentrated, ADH levels rise. Kidneys reabsorb more water and urine becomes dark and concentrated.

twist.text: Alcohol suppresses ADH. That's why drinking beer makes you urinate frequently and wake up dehydrated the next morning.

climax.text: ADH maintains the body's water balance with remarkable precision. Too little and you dehydrate.

punchline.text: One hormone decides if water stays or goes. ADH runs your hydration.

quiz.question: Why does alcohol cause dehydration?
options: It suppresses ADH, causing kidneys to release more water
It increases body temperature, causing sweat loss
